lens: Database and release: schema v2 and seed v2+ against the applied v1, idempotent re-emit, drift guard, production apply, rollback. Experiments: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Sports-genome/1ff0a7bc-72e5-5e41-a8d9-937a97929500/scratchpad/multi-region/critic-db-exp.ts. It applies schema v1, seed v1 and the assembled v2 prototype in PGlite 0.4.6 (Postgres 17.5).

issues.problem: The guard freezes an attribute as soon as any non-draft version maps its variant, even a version published before the attribute existed and that never reads it. Wave 1 ships its attributes with wave A's seed, including those on frozen forearm rows. Each attribute on one of the 98 catalog rows that already has a forearm variant is frozen the moment it is inserted, because forearm_mappings_v1 (18 Oct) maps all of them. That covers the rows, pulldowns, pull-ups, shrugs, hinges and carries that back (wave B) and hips/thigh (wave C) exist to review. Those lanes can then never correct leg_laterality (required by rule 11), stance, knee, grip_width or torso. The only remaining path is cat-<id>.v2 plus a new mapping version for every region that maps the old key, and §3 says none is planned.
issues.evidence: Prototype guard_published_variant_attribute: `where m.variant_key = old.variant_key and v.state <> 'draft'`. Draft:317 (the freeze), :456 (wave 1 'ships with wave A's seed'; '98 of them already have a forearm variant'), :247 (legLaterality required for leg versions), :251 (the v2-key replacement). Experiment 2: cat-205 B-Stance RDL is mapped only by forearm_mappings_v1. Inserting leg_laterality=bilateral and stance=bilateral succeeds. Updating either one right afterwards is refused: 'attribute leg_laterality of variant cat-205 is used by mapping version forearm_mappings_v1 (published); it cannot change or be deleted'. The same happens for stance, with no leg version in existence. 19 frozen hinges, carries and hanging raises are affected (cat-41, 42, 145, 186-189, 202-205, 231, 232, 234, 263, 264, 299, 300, 409).
issues.fix: Freeze what a version actually rested on, recorded at publish. In the restated guard_mapping_version, after the FOR SHARE locks, set `variant_attributes.frozen_at = now()`, or insert a snapshot row, for the attributes present on the version's variants. The attribute guard then refuses change or delete only where frozen_at is not null; frozen_at is not in the seed's upsert columns, so re-applying stays a no-op. Do not compare created_at with published_at: the seed's published_at is the content date at midnight, which is earlier than an attribute inserted in the same apply. Also emit leg-only attributes (leg_laterality, sided_by, stance, knee) in the wave that publishes the first leg region, not with wave A.

issues.problem: Wave A (seed v3) cannot be built or applied as planned. The shoulders list back.upper_trapezius, back.latissimus_dorsi and back.teres_major as external members, but back ships in wave B. Neither those nodes nor a 'back' region row exist at wave A. The seed holds only production and reference regions, and referenceRegionLabels is removed. 'Every wave can ship without the next' is therefore false for wave A.
issues.evidence: Draft:78 (the shoulders' externals), :457-458 (wave A = upper_arm, shoulders, chest; back in B), :461, :197 ('referenceRegionLabels goes'), :341 (the seed holds every production and reference region), :343 (references checked against the merged sets). The emitter today throws 'Node … lives in region …, which is neither … nor a labelled reference region' (emit-seed.ts:278-282). Experiment 4: inserting region_nodes ('shoulders', 'back.latissimus_dorsi', 'external') gives 'violates foreign key constraint "region_nodes_node_id_fkey"'. nodes.region_id → regions would need a back row as well.
issues.fix: Add the three back muscles to the shoulders' members in wave B's seed (v4). Adding a membership to a published region is allowed: the region_nodes guard covers only update and delete. Rule 12 means shoulders_mappings_v1 can never map them, so these memberships never freeze. Add a registry test: every external member's home region is production or reference in the same release. (The other choice, shipping 'back' as a reference region in wave A with three provisional nodes, brings back the reference path the note removes.)

issues.problem: §5.1 adds rule 12 ('every mapped node's home is the version's region') to mapping_version_problems and says forearm_mappings_v1 'is never re-checked against 12'. But §5.3's read-only verification calls mapping_version_problems() on forearm_mappings_v1 and expects null. The function evaluates every rule, so it returns a problem for v1's 53 biceps and brachialis rows, and the production verification step fails. The same holds for any schema test asserting that v1 still passes.
issues.evidence: Draft:328, :359. Experiment 1: rule 12 written as worded and spliced into the prototype function. `select mapping_version_problems(id) … 'forearm_mappings_v1'` → 'mapped muscles whose home is another region: upper_arm.biceps, upper_arm.brachialis'.
issues.fix: Evaluate rules 11 and 12 only for draft versions (`join specialization.mapping_versions v on v.id = p_version_id and v.state = 'draft'`). guard_mapping_version calls the function from a BEFORE UPDATE trigger, while the stored row is still a draft. Tested (experiment 1b): v1 now returns null, and publishing a new forearm draft that maps upper_arm.biceps is still refused with 'mapped muscles whose home is another region: upper_arm.biceps'. Otherwise, change §5.3 to expect exactly that message for v1.

issues.problem: The applied seed v1 is still the emitter's output path, and nothing pins its bytes until lane 0e lands the SHA test and CURRENT_SEED_MIGRATION_PATH. Lane 0a runs first, alone, and changes what the emitter outputs: records move to shared libraries, the registry gains upper_arm, claim and sort derivation change. Its red drift guard tells the agent to run emit-seed, which rewrites the history file. The drift guard then passes, because it only compares the file with the output, so a rewritten v1 goes unnoticed and the repository disagrees with what production ran.
issues.evidence: emit-seed.ts:63 (SEED_MIGRATION_PATH = …_seed_v1.sql) and :740 (writeFileSync). specializationSeed.test.ts:96-104 (the message says 'Run: npx tsx scripts/specialization/emit-seed.ts'). design/specialization/forearm/emit.mjs:7-8 and shared/specialization/regions/forearm/diagram.generated.ts:6 ('regenerate the database seed'). Draft:340-341 (the pin and the path move are in lane 0e), :465 ('0a first; 0b–0f in parallel once 0a's types are merged'), :473. 04-database.md:199.
issues.fix: Land a wave-0 prologue commit before lane 0a. It adds the SHA-256 pin test for both applied files (b67a9cd7…542d, a267fdc4…89f8), points CURRENT_SEED_MIGRATION_PATH at …_seed_v2.sql (the drift guard and --check read it), and rewrites the drift-guard message and the three 'regenerate the seed' notes to name the current file. Lanes then branch from it.

issues.problem: The production apply (step 3) is not ordered after the wave review or after the branch is brought up to date with main. Once production records seed vN it is history, and its published versions, reviewed claims and mapped muscles are frozen. A review finding or a main merge after step 3 therefore cannot regenerate vN. The merged tree then fails the drift guard against the frozen file, and a mapping or claim error is published for good (fixable only with new keys and _v2 versions).
issues.evidence: Draft:497 ('Wave review before each merge'; nothing says before the apply), :499-504 (apply at step 3, squash merge at step 4), :341 ('history from the moment production records it'), :447 ('publishing freezes'). 04-database.md:199.
issues.fix: Write the order into §9.4: the wave review and its fix round finish; main is merged into the wave branch and CI is green on that SHA; the apply runs from that exact SHA; then the squash merge happens with no further commits (branch protection 'require up to date'; no specialization merges to main in between). Any change after the apply goes into the next seed file.

issues.section: §5.1 goals foreign keys / §5.2 'a removed membership is deleted'
issues.problem: Schema v2 makes goals reference region_nodes (region_id, node_id) and region_actions (region_id, action_id), while the seed deletes memberships and region actions the content drops. v1 deliberately never deletes rows that goals point at. Once goals sync (the tables are 'ready for it'), any seed that drops an unmapped, unfrozen member or region action that some user has a goal on fails with an FK error raised by another user's row, and the whole release rolls back. ON DELETE CASCADE would instead silently delete athletes' goals.
issues.evidence: Draft:323, :345. 04-database.md:152 and emit-seed.ts:32 ('never deletes the records others point at … nodes (goals may point at one)'). Experiment 3: a user A goal on the unfrozen member (forearm, forearm.anconeus), then the seed-style stale delete → 'update or delete on table "region_nodes" violates foreign key constraint "goals_node_in_region" on table "goals"'.
issues.fix: Never hard-delete memberships or region actions from the seed. Add `listed boolean not null default true` (or `removed_on date`) to region_nodes and region_actions. The seed sets it false for rows the content drops (still refused when frozen), the RLS policies and the goals trigger accept only listed rows for new goals, and existing goals keep a valid key.

issues.section: §4.3 rule v2 text, published at wave 0
issues.problem: Rule v2 is published, and so immutable, at wave 0, and the forearm page shows its text. Its externals clause says another region's muscle is 'credited as its home region's current mapping version credits it'. From wave 0 until wave A, the forearm page instead credits the biceps and brachialis from the forearm's own 53 rows, the §4.2 fallback, which the rule text never states. The page would contradict its own published rule for a whole wave. The v2 text also freezes midline, leg-limb and opposite/both wording that no production region uses until waves B and C.
issues.evidence: Draft:274-278 (the clauses v2 adds), :266 (the fallback 'read until upper_arm_mappings_v1 is published (wave A)'), :455 (seed v2 carries rule v2; 'the rule's text' visible at wave 0), :282 (the forearm's numbers do not change at wave 0). Schema v1:750-769 (guard_published_rule_version refuses any update or delete once published_at is set).
issues.fix: Write the fallback into v2 ('where the muscle's home region has no published version, the listing region's own reviewed rows credit it'). Since wave 0 changes no forearm number, keep the forearm on v1 at wave 0 and publish v2 with wave A. Add a test that matches each branch of nodeSideFor and of indexRegion's version choice to a clause of the text.

issues.problem: The note gives no rollback for schema v2 or the later seeds. The emitter's header carries 'Rollback: the schema's (drop schema if exists specialization cascade)' into seed v2 and later. After wave 0 that destroys forearm_mappings_v1's published history and any synced goals, and it leaves supabase_migrations.schema_migrations rows for files that are no longer in the database. The new apply refusal ('… and this one is not [recorded]') then refuses to re-apply them. Once seed v3 writes not_applicable variants and publishes versions over them, v1's CHECKs and functions cannot be restored either.
issues.evidence: emit-seed.ts:715. Schema v1:61-64. server/specializationSchema.test.ts:1138-1170 (the rollback test reads the drop line from the v1 file). Draft:356 (the new refusal), :250 (not_applicable), §5.1 (constraints widened in place).
issues.fix: Header of schema v2: forward-only, plus one tested undo that is valid only before seed v3. The undo drops the five tables, the new columns, constraints and triggers; restores v1's mapping_version_problems and guard_mapping_version bodies and the v1 CHECKs; and deletes its own schema_migrations row in the same transaction. Emitter header: replace the drop-schema line with 'forward-only: corrections are new keys in the next seed'. Extend the rollback test to the v2 undo and to the apply refusal after it.

issues.problem: Claim keys are built from the region whose data lists the claim. The note moves the four forearm-owned claims on the biceps and brachialis into regions/upper_arm/claims.ts, but §5.2's emitter changes add no explicit owner. The keys would become upper_arm:biceps.function and so on, and the stale-claim delete (owned prefix 'forearm', key no longer in the content) would try to delete the reviewed forearm:biceps.function. guard_published_claim refuses that, so all of seed v2 fails.
issues.evidence: emit-seed.ts:329-333 (`claimKey(data.region.id, claim.id)` for claims and for node actions), :361-372 (ownClaim delete). Draft:198 (records move, keys stay forearm:), :343-349 (the emitter change list). Schema v1:904-941.
issues.fix: Give Claim a required ownerRegionId and build the key as `${owner}:${id}`. Compute the ownClaim delete over owners, not region files. Add an emitter test that every v1 claim key and node-action claim key comes out byte for byte.

issues.problem: Rule 11 and the new regions guard rely on regions.side_limb, side_model, catalog_keys and region_only_tag_scope, but publishing locks only region_nodes and variant_attributes besides v1's rows. A region update racing the region's first publish sees no non-draft version and passes, while the publish checked rule 11 against the old values. This breaks v1's stated principle that publishing locks everything it rests on FOR SHARE.
issues.evidence: Draft:329 (the locks added), :320 (the regions guard applies only once a non-draft version exists), :328 (rule 11). Schema v1:597-631 (v1's lock list). Reasoned, not tested: PGlite is a single connection (04-database.md §8).
issues.fix: In guard_mapping_version, before mapping_version_problems: `perform 1 from specialization.regions r where r.id = new.region_id for share;`

lens: Correctness of the counting and the data model: double counting across regions, side models (legs, trunk), shared variants vs frozen v1, mapping versions, goals per region, a region-agnostic calculator, migration of existing device data, existing tests. Experiments are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Sports-genome/1ff0a7bc-72e5-5e41-a8d9-937a97929500/scratchpad/multi-region/critic-counting/ (c1–c10, run with npx tsx from the repo root). The repository was not modified.

issues.section: §4.2 Externals credited by their home region (and the 'region-only' bullet); shared/specialization/exposure.ts classifyBout
issues.problem: The draft says two things that cannot both hold. First, an external member is credited by its home region's version, so one set shows the same credit on every page. Second, a bout whose mappings credit only external members, but whose tags carry the region's keys, 'is region-only work'. In the calculator a bout is exactly one of mapped, region_only or unrelated (exposure.ts:54-57). A region_only bout stops before any node gets credit (exposure.ts:387-395). So one of two things happens. Either the external loses its credit on that page, which breaks §4.2's same-credit promise. Or, as the current code does, the bout becomes 'mapped' and drops out of the region-only bucket, which changes the forearm page at wave A.
issues.evidence: c5-external-only.ts, 24 Dumbbell Pullover (tagged forearms and biceps as secondary, not mapped by forearm v1). Today: regionUnclassified 1, boutsRegionOnly 1. With an upper-arm biceps row merged into the forearm index, as §4.2 requires: regionUnclassified 0, boutsRegionOnly 0, boutsWithReviewedMapping 1, biceps credited 1. c3-catalog.ts lists what moves at wave A. Rows 24, 63, 64, 65, 279, 280 and 345 are tagged forearms, left unmapped by the forearm and tagged biceps. Rows 318, 326, 329, 330 and 333 go from unrelated to counted in the forearm's completeness. The same will happen on the chest and shoulders pages through their externals.
issues.fix: Let one bout be both. A mapped bout whose effects touch no own member, and whose tags match under the region's tag scope, still credits its external effects. It also goes into regionUnclassified and boutsRegionOnly, and completeness does not count it under boutsWithReviewedMapping. Add two tests. On every page, an external's row equals its home page's row for the same bouts and side. The forearm's regionUnclassified and boutsRegionOnly at wave A equal wave 0's.

issues.section: §2.1 rules 1 and 5 (midline counting; planned one-sided work); client/src/lib/specialization/planBouts.ts
issues.problem: A planned set of a one-sided exercise is one bout, side 'bilateral', sideSource 'plan_assumption' (planBouts.ts:79-83). By the plan convention it stands for one set per side: '3 × 12 is three sets for each arm' (planBouts.ts:70-77), and the tracker logs it as two rows, Right then Left (perArmSets). For a region paired by that limb this matches. Rule 1 counts every bout once on a midline region, though. A region paired by the other limb reads that one bout as structural. On those pages the planned count is half the logged count. Planned against logged is the page's paired view (design §4), and planned goals read the same bouts.
issues.evidence: c8-plan-vs-log.ts, 409 Suitcase Carry '3 × 30'. Planned: 3 bouts. Logged as the tracker builds it: 6. Forearm, left arm: planned 3, logged 3. Midline under rule 1: planned 3, logged 6. The same gap appears for a Bulgarian split squat with two dumbbells on an arm-paired region once wave C lays rows out per leg, and for side and Copenhagen planks planned per side on the core and the hips.
issues.fix: For a variant that is `unilateral` for its sidedBy limb, planBouts emits two bouts per planned set (`…/n#right`, `…/n#left`), each with its side on that limb and sideSource plan_assumption. nodeSideFor puts each bout on its own side for regions paired by that limb, so the forearm still gets 3 per arm and its planned numbers do not change. Midline and other-limb regions count both bouts. An `either` variant stays one bout. Add a test: planned equals logged-as-built on the core, the back and the forearm for 409, 46, 173 and 247. Extend the golden test to planned summaries, where only bout ids may differ.

issues.problem: The draft moves side resolution to each mapping (nodeSideFor), but only for the rows. §2.2 changes how goals are validated and stored, not how their progress is counted. Goal progress still filters each bout by `goal.side !== request.side` and `onArm(bout, goal.side)` (exposure.ts:485, 492), and only then reads the node's effects. exposure.ts:472 promises that a muscle goal equals the muscle's row bucket. That stops being true: (a) a left-hand suitcase carry credits the right quadratus lumborum in its row (opposite), but a right-QL goal skips the bout because it was recorded left; (b) a one-arm row logged Right credits both erectors (both), but a left-erector goal skips it; (c) on a midline page, onArm(bout, 'midline') passes only bilateral bouts, so every left, right and unknown-side bout that rule 1 counts is missing from the goal.
issues.evidence: exposure.ts:485-506 against draft §2.1 rules 1, 2 and 4 and its own scenario list ('a suitcase carry in the left hand credits the right quadratus lumborum…', 'a side plank with no side recorded counts on the core page'). §2.2 never mentions progress.
issues.fix: Compute goal progress from the same per-node, per-side contributions the rows use. A muscle goal reads the node's bucket for its metric over its own period. A movement goal counts distinct bouts with an own-node contribution on this side whose part has the goal's action and category. Add a test over every §2.1 scenario that the goal value equals the row's bucket, on paired and midline pages, completed and planned.

issues.section: §2.1 Sides, per-mapping resolution; region totals and the ledger
issues.problem: Region totals are kept per bout. A bout goes into regionBouts or regionUnknownSide once for each own node it credits (exposure.ts:419-425). The page adds the two (SpecializationPanel.tsx:390) and says '…and N more had no arm recorded' (:398). Rules 2 and 6 apply per mapping, so one bout can count on a side for one own node and be unknown for another. Example: a one-arm row with no side recorded, where the lat is unknown and the erectors are `both`. That set is then counted twice, and the sentence calls it '1 more'. Separately, Contribution.side and RegionBoutRow.side are the side the bout recorded (exposure.ts:207, 227), and the ledger prints that (MuscleSheet.tsx:150 `sideLabels[row.side]`). The right QL's row from a left-hand carry therefore reads 'Left'.
issues.evidence: exposure.ts:205-227 and 419-425; SpecializationPanel.tsx:390-398; MuscleSheet.tsx:150; draft §2.1 rules 2, 4 and 6 and the scenarios 'one-arm row … both erectors' and 'suitcase carry … right quadratus lumborum'.
issues.fix: Put a bout in the region's unknown-side set only when no own node is credited with it on this side. Contribution gets a `countedSide` from nodeSideFor next to `recordedSide` and the side relation. The ledger labels rows by countedSide and adds a note such as 'left hand: opposite side'. Also make the registry test require that an external's home region is paired by the same limb, unless the listing page is midline: the same-credit promise in §4.2 depends on it, and §1.2's 'tests enforce' covers only the midline case.

issues.problem: Rule 12 inside mapping_version_problems ('every mapped node's home is the version's region') flags the published forearm_mappings_v1, which maps upper_arm.biceps and upper_arm.brachialis. Yet §5.3 requires `mapping_version_problems()` to stay null for forearm_mappings_v1 after the apply. server/specializationSchema.test.ts:880-883 asserts the same, and the new harness replays schema v2 before that test runs. The draft's own sentence 'never re-checked against 12' contradicts its verification step.
issues.evidence: c4-rule12.ts on PGlite: schema v1 + seed v1 + the assembled prototype v2 gives problems = null. With rule 12 added as worded it gives 'mapped muscles whose home is another region: upper_arm.biceps, upper_arm.brachialis'.
issues.fix: Keep rule 12 out of mapping_version_problems. Check it in guard_mapping_version on the draft-to-published change only, with its own refusal message, so mapping_version_problems(forearm v1) stays null and both the test and §5.3 still hold. Add a refusal test: publishing a draft version that maps a node whose home is another region is refused.

issues.section: §2.2 Goals and §10 'no history migration': goals already on the device
issues.problem: Today the forearm page offers 'Set a target' for any selected muscle, external and adjacent ones included. MuscleSheet.tsx:161 renders TargetsEditor for every selected node, the external group can be selected (SpecializationPanel.tsx:296), and validateGoal has no role check. So devices may already hold {regionId: 'forearm', nodeId: 'upper_arm.biceps'} or a target on forearm.anconeus. Under the draft: (a) validateGoal and the new DB trigger refuse muscle goals on non-targets, so these goals can no longer be edited or synced; (b) from wave A the upper-arm page accepts {upper_arm, upper_arm.biceps} next to the old goal, because sameGoalTarget compares regionId (goals.ts:47-49). One muscle then has two active targets for the same side, metric and period, and the grid's 'N targets', the logger gates and TargetsOverview count both; (c) the old goal's progress changes without notice at wave A, because it is now read through the upper arm's version.
issues.evidence: c7-goals.ts: validateGoal returns ok for forearm/upper_arm.biceps and for forearm.anconeus. It also returns ok for upper_arm/upper_arm.biceps saved next to the forearm one.
issues.fix: Wave 0: stop offering targets on non-target members. On read, re-home a muscle goal to its node's home region once that region is in production, keeping its id. Show goals on adjacent nodes as ended or read-only, with a note. Make sameGoalTarget ignore regionId for muscle goals (a muscle has one home), and key the DB exclusion for muscle goals by node. Test with these stored goals. validateGoal's messages should also take the region's side words: goals.ts:62 and 78 say 'arm'.

issues.problem: `laterality` has only bilateral, unilateral and either (types.ts:166; DB check at schema.sql:267). The documented rule (variants.ts:13-17) allows `bilateral` only when both arms work in every set, and `either` only where the catalog leaves it open. Hands-free leg and back exercises have no honest value: 169-172 leg presses and extensions, 194-196 leg curls, 200 and 201, 222, 351, 367 and 368. The draft adds not_applicable to orientation and wrist only. sidedBy defaults to `arm` whenever laterality is not bilateral. Take 170 Single-Leg Leg Press with `either`: it gets sidedBy arm, no arm region maps it, so the logger asks nothing (§2.2), and every set reads 'no leg recorded' on the thigh page forever. Exercises one-sided for both limbs also default to arm: 224 Single-Leg Calf Raise with one dumbbell, 196, 356, 357, 358, 367 and 371-373. The only safeguard is the instruction 'set explicitly'.
issues.evidence: Draft §3, the sidedBy default; §2.2, the question appears only when a production region paired by that limb maps the variant; §5.1, only forearm_orientation and wrist_position gain not_applicable. c9-limbs.ts lists the catalog rows above.
issues.fix: Add `not_applicable` to Laterality and LegLaterality, in TypeScript and in the DB check widened by schema v2. The sidedBy default skips not_applicable. When both limbs are one-sided, an explicit sidedBy is required, and the emitter refuses the variant without one. nodeSideFor treats not_applicable for the page's limb as no side from that limb, and such mappings must use `sideRelation: both`. Add a test: every variant that a leg-paired production region maps with legLaterality other than bilateral has sidedBy leg.

issues.section: §2.1 'A side stored without sideLimb means the arm'; device stores
issues.problem: Reading a missing sideLimb as arm means any path that drops the field turns a leg side into an arm side, silently. The production normalizer keeps only the set fields it knows (deviceWorkoutLog.ts:185-205), and every save rewrites the whole history through it (316-318). Saves happen on every logged set (DeviceWorkoutTracker.tsx:481) and when Home stamps on load (Home.tsx:1067). workoutSwap.ts:141 copies `set.side` alone between exercises, and revision.ts:25 SET_FIELDS leaves the limb out of the cache key. A client still on pre-wave-0 code (a rollback, a long-open tab), or any copy path the change misses, turns a 'Leg · Left' set of 188 into a left-arm grip set for the forearm and a set with no leg for the thigh. Goals and measurements have the same weakness. The stores reload through parseStoredGoal and parseStoredMeasurement (stores.ts:58-67, 143-147) and write back the filtered list (196-203, 212-215), so older code deletes midline goals and girth measurements on its next save.
issues.evidence: deviceWorkoutLog.ts:185-205 and 316-318; stores.ts:58-67, 143-147, 196-203 and 212-215; workoutSwap.ts:138-145; revision.ts:25; draft §2.1 and §10.
issues.fix: Store the leg side in its own field (`legSide: left|right|both`) and keep `side` for the arm, so a dropped field reads as unknown (never counted) rather than as the other limb. In wave 0, before any new shape can be written, make normalizeSet and both stores keep fields and entries they do not understand. Add the limb field to revision.ts SET_FIELDS. Test round trips through the old-shape readers.

issues.section: §9.1 wave 1 'Visible to athletes: Nothing'; §4.3 golden test only at wave 0
issues.problem: Wave 1 adds about 297 library variants, and §3 has one resolver serve bouts and planBouts. Today the forearm builds bouts from forearm variants only (useSpecializationSummary.ts:194-198). sideOf turns an unrecorded side into bilateral whenever the variant is bilateral (bouts.ts:306-311). So at wave 1, every forearm-tagged exercise the forearm leaves unmapped moves from 'no arm recorded' to both arms, history included. That covers the 24 in unmappedForearmTaggedExercises and the other secondary-tagged rows. The release says nothing changes for athletes, and the golden test does not run at that wave.
issues.evidence: c10-library-sides.ts, 3 sets of 190 Good Morning. Today: sides unknown, completeness.boutsUnknownSide 3, region-only rows with no arm 3. With a library cat-190 (bilateral): sides bilateral, 0, 0.
issues.fix: Run the forearm golden test at every release (wave 1, A, B and C) against an explicit list of allowed differences. Then choose: either structural sides of region-only bouts come only from variants the page's own version maps, or wave 1's release states the change.

issues.problem: sharedWithOf groups every reviewed `shared` mapping of the variant that has the same category (exposure.ts:187-194), with no version filter. Under §4.2, a variant's mapping list mixes the page's own version with the externals' home versions. If two versions each mark their own muscles `shared` with the same category on one exercise, the page tells the athlete the work 'cannot be split between them' across regions. Neither version made that claim. The draft does plan shared allocations: the triceps heads now, the pectoral heads likely next.
issues.evidence: exposure.ts:187-194; draft §4.2 ('indexRegion reads, per node, exactly one version', which still merges versions per variant) and §1.2 (allocation: shared).
issues.fix: Group shared partners within one version only (`mapping.versionKey === credited.versionKey`). Test with a fixture in which two versions both mark shared rows on one variant.

issues.section: §3 'replaced, not updated: a new key cat-<id>.v2 … mapped by a new forearm_mappings_v2'
issues.problem: The replacement path assumes the forearm owns the variant, but the variant is shared: other regions' published versions map `cat-<id>`. mappingsByVariant is keyed by variant id (exposure.ts:97-103) and one global resolver returns one id per catalog id. Whichever key it returns, the other key's published rows never match a bout again. Today the resolver always prefers `cat-<id>` (exposure.ts:93; bouts.ts:272), so a `.v2` variant would never be read at all.
issues.evidence: exposure.ts:89-96 and 97-103; bouts.ts:266-277; draft §3.
issues.fix: Either a replacement ships a new version, in the same release, for every region whose current version maps the old key, or the resolver works per mapping version, each version reading the variant key its own rows name. Add a test: every current version's mapped variant ids are the ids the resolver returns for their catalog ids.

issues.section: §3 new fields as variant attributes; §5.1 variant_attributes guard
issues.problem: legLaterality and sidedBy decide counting (rule 3 and the logger's question), but they are stored as variant_attributes. The guard lets a new attribute be added to a variant that a non-draft version maps (§5.1), and sidedBy also has a runtime default (§3). Adding either later changes how a published version counts, with no new version; 188 and 264 are the planned case. The argument 'No published rule reads a descriptive dimension' covers the descriptive dimensions, not these two.
issues.evidence: Draft §3 (sidedBy default; 188 and 264 get attributes) and §5.1 (variant_attributes guard: 'a new attribute may be added').
issues.fix: Write sided_by and leg_laterality explicitly for every variant a production region maps, with no runtime default. Once any non-draft version maps the variant, freeze both values and their absence. Allow the 188 and 264 additions only as a listed exception in the seed, with a test.

issues.problem: §1.2 makes back.upper_trapezius, back.latissimus_dorsi and back.teres_major external members of the shoulders, which ship at wave A. The back's nodes are written by the back's anatomy lane in wave B (§9.1, §9.2), and rule 12 bars shoulders_mappings_v1 from mapping them. At wave A, either the emitter's merged reference check (§5.2) or the region_nodes foreign key fails, or the rows appear as unmapped external muscles. The other cross-region externals ship in the same wave as their home, or the home is already in production.
issues.evidence: Draft §1.2 (Shoulders, external members); §9.1 (wave A: upper_arm, shoulders, chest; wave B: back, core); §5.2 (references checked against merged sets).
issues.fix: Ship the shoulders at wave A without the three back externals, and add those memberships in wave B's seed. This is allowed, because the shoulders' own version does not map them. Add a registry test: every member's home region is production or reference in the same seed.

Experiments: production client built into scratch (critic-phone/dist), served and opened at ?workspace=specialization&region=forearm in headless Chromium emulating an iPhone (viewport, isMobile, hasTouch, device scale 3; not an iPhone, not Safari), seeded with the forearm data from docs/specialization-atlas/evidence/page-final-2026-10-17/capture.mjs. The draft's heading row, its 3 x 3 grid and its side words were mocked in the DOM. The baseline matches 09-page.md (390: drawing top 541, 233 px of drawing visible; 375 with Custom dates and a target: 0 px). Scripts and results are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Sports-genome/1ff0a7bc-72e5-5e41-a8d9-937a97929500/scratchpad/multi-region/critic-phone/ (phone.mjs, lean.mjs, rowswitch.mjs, checks*.json, *.png, size.ts, legs.ts). issues.section: §6.1 Choosing a region on a phone (First screen bullet, heading row)
issues.problem: The first-screen guarantees in §6.1 were measured and do not hold. (a) A 44 px heading row with a bordered Regions toggle costs 20 px whenever there is no Back link, which is the usual case (opened from the tab), because today's h1 is only 24 px tall. (b) Folding Back into the row saves 23-24 px, not 'about 50 px'. (c) With the grid open, the claim 'at 390 x 844 always' fails. (d) The remedy 'its drawing height changes, not the rule' cannot work: the drawing's height does not move its top.
issues.evidence: Measured with the draft row and no Back. 390: drawing on screen 233 -> 213 px. 375 FCU: 73 -> 52. 375 FCU with a target: 48 -> 27. 375 Custom dates and a target: strip bottom 593 -> 614 against the dock at 597, so the strip is no longer whole and the drawing sits 21 px below the screen. That state passes today, so the draft turns a passing state into a failing one, and the draft's '375: every state but Back with Custom dates' is wrong. With Back, Custom dates and a target: 637 -> 614 at 375 and 654 -> 630 at 390. Lean grid (3 rows of 44 px, 144 px in all) open at 390 x 844 with Custom dates and a target: strip bottom 780 against the dock at 774, drawing 12 px below the screen (lean-grid-open-390-custom-target.png). Grid open at 375: the strip is off the first screen in every state (FCU: 691 against 597). Files: checks.json, checks-lean-grid.json.
issues.fix: Replace the claims with a measured table. Treat grid-open as a choosing state: only the toggle and the grid must be on the first screen, and the grid closes on a pick, Escape or a tap on the toggle. Before adopting the 44 px row, win back the 20 px inside .spz-top and re-measure the 375 states with and without Back. One option: tighten the max-height:700px gaps. Another: make the toggle the h1 itself so no extra line is added. Delete 'its drawing height changes'. Content above the drawing sets its top, so the rule must trim that content.

issues.problem: (a) The shoulders' noun does not fit at 375 x 667. 'Left shoulder · Right shoulder' cannot sit beside 'Completed · Planned' and takes a third control row (+52-54 px). (b) The page mixes nouns: the switch says 'Right hip' or 'Right shoulder', while unknown sides say 'no leg/arm recorded' because the logger asks Arm or Leg. (c) Today's templates join the region label to the side noun, which gives 'touched the shoulders on the right shoulder', 'the hips on the right hip' and 'Nothing logged for a muscle of the lower legs on the right leg'. Only the 'Muscles of the …' sentence is tested (§1.1).
issues.evidence: Measured, side words only. 390: controls 102 -> 156 px. 375: drawing on screen 48 -> -4. With the draft row on the shoulders page at 375, a selected muscle with one target: strip bottom 618 against the dock at 597, drawing -25 (shoulders-row-and-switch-375-target.png, checks-row-switch.json). 'Left side', 'Left hip' and 'Left leg' fit on the row. Templates: SpecializationPanel.tsx:397-398 (regionLine), 349-351, 359, 365, 373, 376, 382, 497 ('once per arm'), model.ts:194, 245-246, 302-303.
issues.fix: Take the switch words from the limb the logger asks about. Use 'Left arm · Right arm' for shoulders, upper arm and forearm; 'Left leg · Right leg' for hips, thigh and lower leg; 'Left side · Right side' for chest and back. All of these were measured to fit. Add region wording `onSide(side)` ('your right shoulder', 'the right side of your chest', 'your right lower leg', 'your core'), use it in every sentence that names the region and a side, and drop '{the label} on the {noun}'. Add a test that renders every template for all 9 regions and both sides and refuses a repeated noun and any limb word that does not match the region.

issues.problem: For leg exercises, 'Leg · Left · Right · Both' does not say which leg 'Left' means. On split stances, carries, side lying and Copenhagen work, two readings are equally natural: front foot or elevated rear foot, standing leg or free leg, top leg or bottom leg. The calculator credits the recorded side, or with `opposite` the other side, so a large share of athletes would have every set credited to the wrong leg. A side that is recorded wrongly can never be corrected later, the same reason §11 decision 3 gives for always asking.
issues.evidence: Catalog rows (legs.ts): 173 Bulgarian Split Squat, 174 Front-Foot-Elevated Split Squat, 175-178 lunges, 261/371/373 lunges, 220 Cossack Squat, 188/264 Single-Leg RDL (stance leg against free leg), 217 Copenhagen Plank (top leg on the bench does the adducting), 397 Side Plank Hip Adduction (the bottom leg adducts). The forearm never needed this: 07-logger.md:61 'Arm' is always the hand holding the load.
issues.fix: Add a per-variant `sideAnchor` (working_leg_front, stance_leg, top_leg, bottom_leg, leading_leg), set by the variants lane from the exercise definition. The logger's group label comes from it: 'Front leg · Left · Right · Both', 'Standing leg · …', 'Top leg · …'. Every `sideRelation` is stated relative to the anchor. Add a test that every variant with legLaterality unilateral or either has an anchor. The wave screenshots should include the set card for 173 and 217 at 375 and 390.

issues.problem: Wave A ships shoulders, but the shoulders list back.upper_trapezius, back.latissimus_dorsi and back.teres_major as external members, and their home region (back) ships in wave B. At wave A those node rows do not exist. The seed's merged reference check, the region_nodes foreign key and diagram_paths.node_id (an FK to nodes, schema_v1.sql:225) would all refuse a shoulders drawing or membership that names them. §4.2 has no home version to credit them from (its only exception is the forearm's history). The shoulders' own actions shoulder.extension and scapula.upward_rotation would list only the posterior deltoid and the serratus as movers, which misleads.
issues.evidence: Draft line 78 (shoulders externals) against lines 457-458 (A: upper_arm, shoulders, chest; B: back, core). §7.1: the path-name table includes externals. §5.2: references are checked against the merged sets. Shoulders, chest and back list each other; core lists back.quadratus_lumborum; the three leg regions list each other.
issues.fix: Order the waves by external dependency. A: the upper arm alone. Its only external, forearm.br, is already in production, and it proves promotion, claim ownership and home-region credit. B: shoulders, chest and back together. C: core, after back. D: hips, thigh and lower leg. If back must stay in a later wave, the shoulders ship without the back externals and their actions, and the wave B release re-emits the shoulders drawing as asset version 2. Say which in §9.1.

issues.problem: The work is several times the forearm's, and the plan budgets less review than the forearm needed. Wave A alone carries more mapping decisions and rows than the whole forearm release, plus about 297 new variants in a single lane, three drawings, and only one fix round per lane, although the forearm drawing needed two (§9.3). Nothing in §9 states the counts, so no wave has a realistic scope.
issues.evidence: size.ts, from the catalog and the §1.2 node keys. (catalog row, region) decisions the §3 coverage test demands (a mapping or a listed reason): 1,225 against the forearm's 137 tagged rows. Estimated mapping rows: 1,983-2,867 against 418. Wave A: 501 decisions, 759-1,081 rows. B: 359, 522-690. C: 365, 702-1,096. Thigh alone: 398-568 rows. Drawings: 41 view-layers in §7.2 against the forearm's 7 (hit-targets.json). Forearm content: 418 rows, 63 distinct rationales, 397 of them anatomy or inference.
issues.fix: Put the counts in §9.1 for each wave. Ship one region per release until the second region has gone through review: the upper arm first, about 194 decisions. Split each mapping lane by exercise family (presses, pulls, squat/hinge, isolation), with about 250 rows per review. Budget two fix rounds for each drawing lane. Run the variants work per wave (see the variants finding).

issues.section: §7.2 Views and layers against §1.2 layers and the §7.3 contract
issues.problem: The view and layer table contradicts the node layers in §1.2 and the outcrop rules the contract keeps, so several planned drawings cannot pass their own tests. (1) Thigh Back has only surface and deep, but semimembranosus (a target) and adductor magnus (an external) are intermediate. Semimembranosus would be drawn nowhere, and the 'semimembranosus outcrops' note is impossible. (2) Shoulders: infraspinatus and teres minor are `surface` in §1.2 but called 'window outcrops'. An outcrop must belong to a deeper layer. (3) Upper arm: 'brachialis outcrop between biceps and triceps' belongs on the Outer side, which has only a surface layer. An outcrop must be cut from the whole muscle on its own layer in the same view. (4) Lower leg Outer side has surface and deep. No lower-leg node is deep from the lateral side, and soleus (intermediate, visible laterally) has no middle layer there, so it cannot be drawn. (5) Deltoid, pectoralis major, trapezius and triceps are kind `muscle` with role `group`. §7.3 makes them drawable and model.ts:126-127 makes them selectable. Drawn, they overlap their heads. Selected, they carry no mapping and would read 'Mapping not reviewed'.
issues.evidence: forearmDiagram.test.ts:141 (belly only on its own layer), :160 (`expect(node.layer).toBe("deep")` for outcrops), :169 (outcrop cut from its own muscle 'in the same view'). Draft lines 116-118, 166-171, 410-417, 423.
issues.fix: Generate the view and layer plan from §1.2 and add contract tests. Every target is drawn whole on its own layer in at least one view. A view that holds an outcrop has that node's own layer. No layer is drawn without a node. A node that is any node's parent is neither drawable nor selectable. Fixes: thigh Back gets surface, middle and deep. Infraspinatus and teres minor become deep with partial surface visibility, or the 'outcrop' wording goes. Upper-arm Outer side gets a deep layer, or the outcrop moves to Front. Lower-leg Outer side becomes surface and middle.

issues.problem: Some planned layers add no node, or repeat another view, at the cost of drawing and review rounds and of more taps on a phone. Shoulders Side-deep shows only supraspinatus, which Back-deep already shows. The core Side view repeats Front's three layers (external oblique, internal oblique, transversus) and adds only quadratus lumborum, a back node the back drawing already draws. A side view also shows one flank, which contradicts the core's 'both sides, never mirrored'. Lower-leg Outer side-deep has no node (see the previous finding).
issues.evidence: Draft §1.2 layers: shoulders (supraspinatus is the only deep node visible from the side), core (4 nodes on 3 layers, plus QL external), lower leg. §7.2 table lines 410, 414, 417.
issues.fix: Drop shoulders Side-deep, drop the core Side view (Front on surface, middle and deep covers all four core targets; QL stays in the list and on the back drawing), and replace lower-leg Outer side-deep as above. That cuts about 5 of 41 view-layers. Keep a written reason for every remaining view in each region's diagram note.

issues.section: §9.2 Wave 1 variants lane, §3 legLaterality/dims, §5.1 variant_attributes guard
issues.problem: The variants lane runs only in wave 1, but the leg attributes freeze long before anyone reviews legs. legLaterality (required by rule 11), sidedBy, and the knee and stance dimensions are written in wave 1 and become frozen once any non-draft version maps the variant. Forearm-mapped variants freeze as soon as the attribute is added. Wave A maps split-stance presses. Both happen before the wave C leg lanes review them. And 'a missing variant is a request to this lane' has no lane to go to in waves B and C.
issues.evidence: §5.1: 'an attribute of a variant a non-draft version maps cannot change or be deleted'. §3: 188 and 264 get legLaterality and sidedBy as attributes on frozen rows. Catalog: 302 Split-Stance Cable Chest Press (chest primary, glutes secondary) and 386 Landmine Split Press (frontDelts and triceps primary; quads and glutes secondary) are mapped in wave A.
issues.fix: Run a variants lane in every wave, owning only the attributes that wave's regions read. Attributes are add-only, so deferring them is safe: leg attributes and anchors are written in the legs wave and reviewed with the leg mappings, and midline-relevant ones with the core. Each wave's lane also takes missing-variant requests.

issues.problem: Several files are owned by one lane while the work on them belongs to another. (1) shared/specialization/loggingPolicy.ts is 0b's, but the policy changes in §6.4 (askSide by sidedBy, sideLimb, oneSide) are the logger's (0c). (2) Home.tsx is 0d's, but 0c's loggerGatesFor(goals) has to be wired where Home computes askStraps and perArmSets. (3) viewState.ts is 0b's, but withRegion and the region memory belong to the picker (0d). (4) ActionGlyph.tsx falls under 0d's components glob, but §7.3's new glyph kinds are 0f's. (5) regions/forearm/logging.ts (0a's glob) is replaced by 0c's generated table. (6) In waves A-C the drawing lane builds path ids from short names (asset.mjs:59-62, NODE_FOR_SHORT_NAME), and the outcrop test reads surfaceVisibility. Both are written by the anatomy lane, and §1.2 does not fix short names, so 'anatomy, mapping and drawing in parallel' rests on fields that are still moving.
issues.evidence: Draft lines 470-474, 483-485, 62. Home.tsx:570 (askStraps) and :2307 (askStraps and perArmSets passed to the tracker). loggingPolicy.ts:1-60. regions/forearm/logging.ts. forearmDiagram.test.ts:160-161.
issues.fix: Move loggingPolicy.ts and regions/forearm/logging.ts to 0c. Give 0c a named Home.tsx hunk, sequenced after 0d, or have 0d wire 0c's exported API. Move withRegion in viewState.ts to 0d and ActionGlyph.tsx to 0f. In §1.2, fix each node's short name, matching [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9-]* and unique within its drawing, externals included. The anatomy lane lands nodes.ts (layer, visibility, short name) and nodeActions.ts as a first checkpoint before the drawing and mapping lanes finish.

issues.problem: Two things the athlete needs to be told are not said. (1) With region-only scope 'primary', any secondary-tagged row the core (or any region) lists as unmapped vanishes from the page entirely: it is not credited and not region-only. Those rows include the squat, deadlift, bench and overhead press, and the core alone has 189 of them. `unmappedTagged` is test data the page never shows. An athlete who squats and deadlifts every week can be told 'No exercise logged in this window loads a mapped muscle of the core'. (2) The §8 statement covers how review was done, but not what a reviewed mapping rests on. Most rows are joint-action anatomy or inference, not a measurement on that exercise.
issues.evidence: exposure.ts:152-155 (no matching key -> 'unrelated'). SpecializationPanel.tsx:552 (the 'No exercise … loads a mapped muscle' line). size.ts: 1,225 decisions, 675 of them secondary-only rows. Forearm content: 176 anatomy + 221 inference + 21 EMG of 418 rows. regions/forearm/mappings.ts:339-342 holds the forearm's methodNotes, and §8 does not require one per region.
issues.fix: Add a completeness count and a list for listed-unmapped rows the athlete actually did: 'N sets tag the core as a secondary muscle and are not counted here', each with its reason, opened from 'How this is counted'. Require each region's mapping version to carry methodNotes that say plainly that a reviewed mapping means the muscle does that joint action in that exercise, from anatomy references, and not how much the exercise loads it. Say the same for incidental 'bracing', 'balance' and 'steadying' credit.
